newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK govt paper yields up but buying interest strong.
newsitem.headline: HK govt paper yields up but buying interest strong.

text.p: Hong Kong government paper yields rose on concerns of a possible U.S. monetary tightening, but strong buying interest kept the decline in prices small relative to U.S. treasuries, traders said.
The seven-year Exchange Fund note yielded 7.66 percent versus 7.48 at Friday midday, five-year yielded 7.30 against 7.11, and three-year 6.69 against 6.53. Monday was a holiday.
The one-week bill yielded 4.98 percent versus 4.90.
"There was surprisingly strong buying, possibly because players back from summer holidays are rebuilding positions," said a regional bank dealer.
"Yields are attractive here even though everybody is talking about another Fed tightening."
It remained to be seen if buying would continue,he added.

Minutes from the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee's July 2-3 meeting, released on Friday, revived fears of higher interest rates, pushing the U.S. long bond down 18/32 overnight to yield 7.00 percent, its highest level in almost four weeks.
The interbank market was quiet with rates little changed.
Overnight cash stood at 5-1/4 3/16 percent versus 5-5/16 9/32 percent on Friday, while three-month was at 5-17/32 15/32 percent against 5-1/2 15/32 percent.-- JONATHAN SPRAGUE
